current_task: EBOOK GENERATOR RECOVERY SPRINT: provider-routing fix (v1.7.8) held on the next live build. A NEW, unrelated failure surfaced at the manuscript QA/approval step, now fixed in v1.7.9, commit ca33aa0, pushed to origin/main, pending the owner's live re-test -- this is the third consecutive fix pending live proof. Live build "Container Gardening Step by Step" advanced past chapter generation (proving v1.7.8's fix works) and failed with 'Resolve structural/content findings before approving the manuscript.' on attempt 1, then 'Cannot approve an empty manuscript.' on attempt 2. ROOT CAUSE (one defect, two symptoms): services/ebook_build_orchestrator.py::_run_manuscript called approve_stage() directly after generation, which always raises when the stage needs correction, without ever invoking the Factory's existing execute_correct_manuscript() correction system; and advance_build()'s exception handler persisted the STALE pre-attempt data snapshot on any failure, silently erasing the assembled manuscript and all persisted chapter progress the runner had already saved, forcing a full re-billed regeneration on the very next attempt -- which is exactly why attempt 2 landed on a completely different, worse outcome (non-deterministic regeneration produced zero passing chapters instead of the same findings again). FIX: _run_manuscript now runs the existing correction pass automatically once before approving (a resumed NEEDS_CORRECTION draft goes straight to correction, generation is never re-triggered over it); explicit checkpoint persists were added before approve_stage runs; advance_build's exception handler now re-reads the database before recording a failure instead of overwriting it. No second correction system was built. Full Release Gate: 2869 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, 0 paid API calls. Fast Gate: 160 passed, 698 subtests. No LOCKED function shares the changed files. STILL OPEN: the owner must run a live ebook build; success means it advances past 30% (manuscript approved) into visuals/cover/design and ultimately reaches export-ready. Upgrade 2 still requires the owner's explicit approval and is not started by this fix.
stopped_at: Read-only trace first, per the recovery sprint's explicit requirement: confirmed generation had genuinely produced content (attempt 1's error requires non-empty content, per approve_stage's own check order) and that the structural/content findings were real, not stale validation -- then traced attempt 2's 'empty manuscript' to a single, confirmed mechanism rather than treating the two attempts as separate bugs. Found via direct code reading: advance_build's except-block called database.update_project(project_id, None, data) using `data` captured BEFORE the stage runner ran, unconditionally, on every failure -- discarding whatever the runner's own persist_progress callback had already saved during that same attempt, and discarding the runner's own return value entirely (never used on the failure path). Separately found that _run_manuscript never checked for an existing NEEDS_CORRECTION draft before calling execute_generate_manuscript, and never invoked services.ebook_project_workspace.execute_correct_manuscript at all -- an existing, fully-built correction system (the same one used for a human-triggered 'Request Correction') that was simply never wired into the automatic build. Implemented three coordinated, minimal fixes: (1) _run_manuscript checks for an existing NEEDS_CORRECTION draft and skips straight to correction on a resumed attempt, never re-triggering generation over it; (2) _run_manuscript explicitly persists the assembled manuscript/QA state as a checkpoint immediately after generation and after correction, before approve_stage runs, since chapter-level persist_progress alone does not cover that final assembly step; (3) advance_build's exception handler re-reads the database's current state before recording a failure, so recording a failure can only add information, never erase already-saved progress. Added persist_progress support to execute_correct_manuscript for the same interruption-safety guarantee execute_generate_manuscript already had. Built tests/test_ebook_manuscript_correction_recovery.py (6 tests, zero paid calls): the centerpiece uses the Factory's own real acceptance-project fixture (10 real chapters, real validators) with only the chapter-writing function replaced, proving 9 already-good chapters are called exactly once each while the one genuinely flawed chapter is repaired automatically (called twice: fail, then fix) and the build advances from 30% to 40%; five more tests pin the exact failure shape at the orchestration-wiring level (findings trigger correction and the result is re-reviewed; a rejected manuscript's content and accepted chapters survive; a resumed NEEDS_CORRECTION project goes straight to correction without regenerating; a genuinely empty manuscript still fails clearly). Followed the required proof order: targeted tests -> 189 + 188 broader manuscript/ebook tests -> Fast Stability Gate (160 passed, 698 subtests) -> Full Release Gate (2869 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, 0 paid API calls) -- never running the Full Gate first. Committed as ca33aa0 and pushed to origin/main.

items: The owner ran a NEW live ebook build after the v1.7.7 fix deployed and got the identical failure -- proving that fix's RENDER-environment-variable check did not actually engage in the real deployed runtime. The owner explicitly stopped this session from assuming success just because tests passed, and required proof from a fresh live traceback before any further change.

New live traceback confirmed: services.ai_providers.ProviderUnavailable: Local engine unreachable at http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat: Connection refused -- same generate_one_chapter call chain, meaning select_provider() still chose LocalAIProvider in production despite v1.7.7's RENDER check.

Traced why: v1.7.7's _running_on_render() rested on an unverified assumption (that the hosting platform auto-injects a RENDER variable) that the live evidence disproved for this deployment. Ruled out other candidates directly: no other call path bypasses routes_local(); provider selection is not cached ahead of the policy check; .env does not define RENDER, so dotenv override was not the mechanism for that specific variable.

Rather than attempt a third detection method, changed the actual default: services/ai_providers.py's DEFAULT_POLICY is now POLICY_PREMIUM (cloud), not POLICY_LOCAL_FIRST. Local chapter generation is opt-in ONLY -- FACTORY_AI_POLICY must be explicitly 'local_first' or 'local_only' -- so a missing, wrong, or not-carried-forward setting means cloud, on any hosting platform, without needing to recognize it. Removed the RENDER-detection code from v1.7.7 entirely.

Preserved local Windows Ollama support: added the one explicit opt-in line to the owner's own .env (gitignored, not committed) and documented the same contract in .env.example with an explicit warning never to set it on a hosted deployment.

Updated tests/test_ai_providers.py's baseline fixture to the new opt-in contract and added the core production-safety test proving a missing policy defaults to premium, never local. Rewrote tests/test_ai_provider_render_safety.py (10 tests) for the corrected mechanism.

While rewriting these tests, found and fixed a real test-infrastructure bug of the exact same shape as the production incident: ai_client.py's own load_dotenv(override=True) fired mid-test via a lazy first import, silently re-injecting .env's FACTORY_AI_POLICY after the test's own cleanup -- fixed by importing ai_client at module level.
